thread:
laura_sales: FYI -- POC with FinSoft failing auth. Customer sees 401s and `invalid_organization` in logs. Can SE + eng triage?

mike_se: thanks laura. can you paste the exact curl and response? also which env (hosted/dedicated) are they on?

laura_sales: hosted. they said they used the API key from the onboarding email. here's the error they pasted: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "invalid_key",
  "message": "API key not valid for organization: org_12345"
}
```

raj_eng: quick thought: looks like a token-organization binding issue. keys issued for one org won't work for requests that declare another org via header or project scope. do they include an `X-Redwood-Org` header or `organization` param?

laura_sales: customer sent this curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-abc' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-mini","input":"hello"}'
```
no extra headers. they say the key came from onboarding console under their company workspace.

raj_eng: hmm. two possibilities: 1) the key is for a different org (maybe a demo org we spun up), 2) their workspace has org/project binding rules and the key is scoped to project `proj-xyz` but they're hitting an endpoint expecting `org_12345`. ask for the key id (we can check binding on our side).

mike_se: @raj_eng can you query key metadata if laura dumps the last 6 chars? I'll ping the customer to share safely.

laura_sales: shared via secure note: key ends with `-d7f9`.

deploybot: API key metadata lookup: sk-live-****-d7f9 -> bound_org: org-demo-templates, scopes: [chat,embeddings], created_by: laura_sales, environment: hosted

raj_eng: confirmed: key is bound to `org-demo-templates`, not the customer's `org_12345`. that's why the service returns `invalid_organization`.

mike_se: ok. simplest fix: generate a new key from the customer's workspace (Support can create a short-lived key if they can't access console). Alternatively, create a cross-org test key but that's discouraged.

laura_sales: customer is asking about pricing impact if we issue an ephemeral key for POC vs upgrading to Dedicated. they want to understand rate limits too.

tess_support: for hosted POC keys we have default rate limit 60 rps and token throughput per plan. Ephemeral keys follow same usage billing; no discount. Dedicated pricing and throughput are quoted separately — I'll loop in pricing.

mike_se: actionable items: 1) tess_support to create a time-limited key bound to org_12345 (exp 48h) and share secure link. 2) laura_sales to confirm they test and paste any new 401/429. 3) raj_eng to monitor logs for any further `invalid_scope` or `rate_limit` errors.

tess_support: creating key now, will post secure link in 1:1.

(20 minutes later)

laura_sales: confirmed customer tested with the new ephemeral key -> success, chat call returned 200 and tokens consumed. :tada:

mike_se: great. raj, any follow-up on the binding UX so this doesn't repeat? simple doc pointer maybe.

raj_eng: yeah, we should add a note in onboarding: "ensure API key is created under customer's workspace/org — keys are org-bound". I'll file a tiny doc PR after this.

laura_sales: customer also asked about why their earlier requests showed 429 client-side even after 401s. they were retrying quickly and hit the per-key burst limit. resolved after new key.

tess_support: FYI, if teams expect heavy POC load we recommend temporarily raising burst limits or moving to Dedicated trial — pricing contact: @pricing_ops.

mike_se: closing this thread. tl;dr: wrong org-bound key used -> issued ephemeral org-bound key -> POC passed. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
